dedupe_keys.name: designsafe data depot repository nheri natural hazards engineering data including rapid reconnaissance

description: The Data Depot Repository (DDR) of DesignSafe, the cyberinfrastructure of the NSF-funded Natural Hazards Engineering Research Infrastructure (NHERI), is an open-access, self-publishing repository for datasets, documentation, research software and reports from natural hazards research, assigning DOIs to published work and tracking usage and citations. It has operated since 2016, holds legacy data from about 2005 from the earlier Network for Earthquake Engineering Simulation (NEES), and is hosted at the Texas Advanced Computing Center. The NHERI RAPID Facility, another part of the network, supplies reconnaissance instruments and training and reports more than 200 reconnaissance missions and 160 publications using RAPID data. Coverage: natural hazards research projects on earthquakes, windstorms, tsunamis and related water hazards. Access: open browsing and download of published data; publishing requires an account and agreement to community norms. Licence: per publication, under the DDR Data Usage Agreement. Caveats: formats and quality vary by project, and users must respect each publication's licence and restrictions. Simulation uses are observed damage, test and reconnaissance data for calibrating building fragility and regional loss models. Related records: StEER reconnaissance datasets on DesignSafe and the SimCenter R2D tool.
